comments.content: This write is no longer gated on the install having actually happened. `AndroidInstaller.install` returns `DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM` (it only fires the system intent), so on the default, non-root path `DetailsViewModel.installAsset` → `saveInstalledAppToDatabase(isUpdate = true, installOutcome = DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM)` calls `updateInstalledAppVersion` *before* the user confirms in the system installer. If the user cancels, this branch still stores `skippedReleaseTag = latestVersion` and `isUpdateAvailable = false`, permanently hiding an update nobody declined (the app then also reports the older tag as installed, and `checkForUpdates` keeps it suppressed until a strictly newer release appears). That is precisely the case the removed `installOutcome == InstallOutcome.COMPLETED` guard used to prevent. Only the silent Shizuku/root backend returns `COMPLETED`, so gating the skip on the install being confirmed (e.g. skip while `isPendingInstall`, or clear it when the pending install never lands) would preserve the old safeguard while still covering the completed path.

Content: On Android the default installer returns DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM (AndroidInstaller.install), so saveInstalledAppToDatabase → updateInstalledAppVersion runs before the user confirms in the system dialog. A cancelled install therefore still writes skippedReleaseTag = latestVersion and isUpdateAvailable = false, permanently hiding an update the user never declined — the exact case the removed `installOutcome == InstallOutcome.COMPLETED` guard prevented. Suggest gating the skip write (e.g. only when the install is confirmed/not pending) or clearing it when the install never lands.

When the two disagree, an install the user was never warned about still writes a permanent skip. Consider aligning the gate with the same code-first rule (or only recording the skip when the user was actually warned).

comments.content: The code-first branch of `latestStillNewer` answers "still newer?" from `latestVersionCode` alone, so `isUpdateStillAvailable` can now be `true` while `app.latestVersion` is null — the old `!snapshotLatestVersion.isNullOrBlank()` term made that impossible. `latestVersionCode` can be non-null with a null `latestVersion`, because this very function sets `latestVersionCode = newVersionCode` (below) without touching `latestVersion`. Concretely: forward-install a newer release while `latestVersion` is still null (this writes `latestVersionCode`), then roll back to an older build: `movedBackToOlder` is true but there is no tag to record in `skippedReleaseTag`, and `latestCode > newVersionCode` makes `isUpdateStillAvailable` true. Downstream that leaves an "update available" row with no name — `SmartInstallButton` renders `Res.string.update_to_version` with `installedApp.latestVersion` (prints `null`), and `AppItemMapper` falls back to the installed-version label. Keeping the flag dependent on a detected release tag preserves the previous behaviour without affecting the code-first verdict:
